title: Move Fast Break Nothing: Dedy Kredo
talk_summary: A Codium AI demo pitching a GAN-inspired 'generator + critic' architecture: one component generates code/tests, a separate 'code integrity' critic maps behaviors, generates tests, reviews PRs, and reflects on failures to auto-fix. The concrete mechanisms are behavior-based test generation, run-and-autofix reflection loops, and a PR review/score step that flags security issues like leaked API keys.

takeaways.what_they_do: The critic component maps a class's behaviors (happy path, edge cases, sub-behaviors), generates a test suite for selected behaviors, then code enhancements are applied only after tests exist to protect the change.
takeaways.evidence_quote: it basically Maps out different behaviors and it starts generating tests

takeaways.technique: Run-and-autofix reflection loop on failing tests
takeaways.what_they_do: When a generated test fails, the model reflects on the failure and generates a fix, then reruns; they show it passing on the second attempt.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the model actually analyzes reflects on the failure and then it tries to generate a fix in an automated manner

takeaways.technique: PR review with explicit score plus security scan
takeaways.what_they_do: A slash-review step summarizes the PR, gives it a score, and flags potential security vulnerabilities such as a leaked API key, then offers an 'improve' fix.
takeaways.evidence_quote: it will summarize the pr it will give it a score ... it does introduce a a potential security vulnerability

takeaways.what_they_do: They argue for a GAN-like system split: one component generates code, a distinct 'code integrity' component reviews and probes edge cases, rather than one model doing both.
takeaways.evidence_quote: two different components one focused on the code generation piece and one that serves as the critic

takeaways.what_they_do: They track which behaviors (happy path, edge cases) are covered by tests rather than raw code-coverage percentage.
takeaways.evidence_quote: behavior coverage is a more useful metric than actual code coverage
